query:
ONE QUESTION: Does this SessionRouter change satisfy Trey's law "boundary-flat is proven at the broker, never in the ledger" without violating his doctrine — and if not, name the exact line that breaks it?

Doctrine constraints the change must honor: (1) windDownFlattenComplete becomes true ONLY on broker [] — never on state count; (2) broker legs unknown to state (ghost class) are flattened through the SAME _closeSourceTradeThroughExecution/executeTrade path as tracked trades, tagged STALE_BROKER_ORPHAN, max-loud trace + ntfy; (3) broker read rejection = unverifiable, boundary does NOT cross, failed-safe governs, process alive — "unreachable != flat"; (4) both transition directions; (5) REUSE the existing _fetchBrokerRestSnapshot reconcile, no duplicate reader; (6) NO new gate, flag, config knob, or throw; (7) fail loud, never shut the bot down; each orphan handled as its own cell.

parsed.disagreement: Mercury/Fable claim that orphans are "flattened through the SAME _closeSourceTradeThroughExecution/executeTrade path as tracked trades" is only proven against a mocked executeTrade; the real _closeSourceTradeThroughExecution body (its state lookups, exitPrice handling when getExitPrice returns null, and any activeTrades.get(tradeId) assumptions) is never shown or exercised, so the ghost-class path is asserted, not demonstrated.
parsed.requiredRecheck: core/SessionRouter.js — full body of _closeSourceTradeThroughExecution (verify no activeTrades/state-manager lookup rejects or misroutes a tradeId absent from state, and what happens when getExitPrice returns null); core/NtfyTraceNotifier.js:105-114 (verify RECONCILIATION substring -> ntfy priority max); run `npx jest test/session-router-stock-symbol-config.test.js` on the pre-change commit to prove the 1 failure is pre-existing; confirm _fetchBrokerRestSnapshot exists pre-change and is reused unmodified.
parsed.recheckPrompt: "Verify the broker-proof wind-down receipt with repo tools: (1) paste the full body of _closeSourceTradeThroughExecution and prove a tradeId with no state record (STALE_BROKER_ORPHAN:*) flows to executeTrade without a state lookup throwing, mis-sizing, or skipping — including behavior when getExitPrice returns null; (2) show core/NtfyTraceNotifier.js lines 105-114 and confirm the RECONCILIATION substring maps to ntfy priority max; (3) run `git stash && npx jest test/session-router-stock-symbol-config.test.js && git stash pop` (or check out e1fcc322) to prove the stock-symbol-config failure pre-exists this change; (4) confirm _fetchBrokerRestSnapshot is the pre-existing reconcile reader and is called unmodified; (5) run the full session-router suite and the new broker-proof suite and paste raw output."
parsed.nextCheck: Read the real _closeSourceTradeThroughExecution body in core/SessionRouter.js and trace an orphan tradeId (absent from stateManager.activeTrades) through it to executeTrade — that is the single point where the ghost-class claim can silently break.
parsed.citedReasoning: The diff as presented satisfies constraints (1)-(7) on its face — broker-only proof, ghost class via the shared execution path, unverifiable-read failed-safe, both directions, reused snapshot reader, no new knobs/throws, per-orphan cells. But the answer is a Fable-authored receipt with Mercury unavailable and zero iterations: there is no Mercury verification of the cited test results, the pre-existing-failure attribution (a0afdc81 rename claim), the NtfyTraceNotifier.js:105-114 RECONCILIATION-substring-to-ntfy-max claim, or the assertion that _closeSourceTradeThroughExecution accepts this orphan shape without state lookups. The most load-bearing unproven claim is that _closeSourceTradeThroughExecution -> executeTrade works for a trade with no state record (no activeTrades entry, no entry metadata) — the probe mocks executeTrade, so the real internal logic of _closeSourceTradeThroughExecution (price lookup, state reads, journal writes) is never exercised against an orphan. That is exactly where a ghost-class flatten would break in production while passing the suite.
